findings.title: A balance reading begun before Remove wallet finishes under the next phrase's wallet: it's shared with the new wallet's Home, kept as its reading, and its private UTxOs are sealed into the new wallet's history
findings.scenario: Wallet A holds 1,200 ₳ private and 300 ₳ public on account 0. Wallet B is another phrase the same user keeps, or someone else's on a shared browser, with 0 ₳. The wallet holds one phrase at a time, so switching phrases means Remove wallet and then restore. (1) A's Home starts a reading. The contract part comes back fast: on mainnet the private index answers it. The account's credential_utxos (or account_addresses) is slow: Koios-only, or the data layer's public part held on Koios, with a 45 s timeout, a retry, and 429 holds of up to 60 s. (2) Within that time the user removes A (Settings → Remove wallet, types the words) and restores B by pasting B's phrase and setting a password, about 20–30 s. (3) B's Home asks for balances. Nothing is kept yet and the key is `mainnet:0`, the same as A's, so `shared()` hands B's Home A's pending promise. When it resolves, B's Home shows A's 1,200 ₳ private balance and A's Seedelfs, plus A's public side and staking (or B's UTxOs with A's staking, if the stall was at account_addresses). Refresh returns the same promise while A's read is still pending. (4) A's read ends under B's keys. Its only check is `keys.account !== index`, and both are 0, so `keep()` writes A's reading, A's account UTxOs and A's addresses into B's session. Until a fresh reading, B's Home, the UTxOs screen and Public activity (which reads Koios by the kept addresses) show A's money as B's. (5) `activity.arrived(network, view.owned)` then seals A's private UTxOs into B's `history.<net>` record as received payments. They stay in B's private Activity after any Refresh, and a different person restoring B reads A's private receipts (amounts and tx hashes). No funds move: Send and the private flows read fresh with B's keys. The harm is wrong figures, a persistent false history, and A's private side shown to whoever restores next.
findings.since: 1f22d431 (2026-09-23, before 1.0.0) for the shared in-flight reading; the account-only keep check since 4279db80 (1.2.0's release review)
findings.evidence: balances.ts:211 `const key = `${network}:${account}``, with no wallet in it. :214 `this.shared(this.inFlight, key, () => this.read(network, account))`. :218-225 `shared()` returns any pending promise under that key. :358-401 `read()`: the network parts run outside the queue (:363-371, `readAccountUtxos(...)`, `readContractView(...)`, `readStake(...)`). The final `wallet.withKeys` (:376) checks only `if (keys.account !== index) return { balances, unkept };` (:392), then `keep(session, network, balances, utxos, addresses)` (:395), then `await this.deps.activity?.arrived(network, view.owned)` (:399) whatever the check said. account.ts:114 runs `discoverAccount` with whichever keys are current after `accountAddresses` returns. activity.ts:427-470 `arrived` → `update` (:627-639) reads and writes `history.<net>` under the current store key, with no wallet identity. Nothing resets BalanceService on Remove: handlers.ts:254-282 (reset-wallet) calls `wallet.reset()` and `ctx.sessions.reset()` (:277) only, and `inFlight` (balances.ts:124) is a field of the long-lived service built once in sw.ts:192. Wallet.reset (wallet.ts:473-480) clears session storage and frees the keys, but an awaited fetch is untouched. A's read fails only if one of its `withKeys` calls lands in the no-wallet window. If the stalled Koios call returns after B's `create()` → `open()` (wallet.ts:657-666), every later call runs under B. The codebase handles this class elsewhere: contract-scan.ts:132-138 and :230-234 (`same(keys)`: 'a lock (or another wallet restored) partway through ends the read, with nothing kept'); sessions.ts:1514-1519 (`reset()`, C16: a scan under way 'writes nothing into the next phrase's book'); runs.ts:77-78 and lovejoin.ts:7238 (`unlockedAt` compared before sending). accounts-switch-reading.test.ts pins only an account switch, where the key differs. Window: koios.ts:429 TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000, :421 RETRY_DELAYS_MS, :497 MAX_BACK_OFF_MS = 60_000; the comment at koios.ts:425-427 notes a credential_utxos over an account with history 'can take tens of seconds on the public tier'. A test could show it: accounts-switch-reading.test.ts's `holdKoios(t, "account_addresses")`, a contract UTxO owned by phrase A, `t.wallet.reset()` + `t.wallet.create(phraseB)`, a `balances.get` started then, release; then assert B's `seedelf.balances.preprod` and B's sealed `history.preprod` hold A's UTxOs. No command run (finder).
findings.fix: Tie each reading to the wallet it began under, as contract-scan's `same(keys)` does. Capture the `Keys` object, or an epoch the Wallet bumps in `open()` and `wipe()` (or `unlockedAt()`), at the start of `reading()`/`read()`. Put it in the in-flight key (`${network}:${account}:${epoch}`). In the final `withKeys`, keep nothing, and skip `activity.arrived` and the failure note (balances.ts:160-165), when it changed. Add `balances.reset()` beside `ctx.sessions.reset()` in handlers.ts reset-wallet, clearing `inFlight`, `inFlightPrivate` and `failedWords`. The same family, to check against the epoch: `readPrivate` (balances.ts:249-280); dapp.ts `view()`'s shared `reading` map (dapp.ts:1614-1623, keyed by network and account); accounts.ts `discover`/`check` → `merge` (:260-322: a look that spans Remove + restore merges the old phrase's used indices into the new phrase's record, which is harmless but the same shape). Activity.cardano is already safe: its pages are reused only for the same key set (activity.ts:507).
findings.known_check: Searched docs/backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/*.md (and docs/*.md) for: in flight, inFlight, 'another phrase', 'next phrase', 'other phrase', 'wallet is removed', 'removed and restored', 'phrase it started', C11, C16, Remove wallet, restore. Found only C16 (the restore scan let go at Remove, fixed: keys-and-accounts.md:88, chunk-27 plan) and the account-switch reading fix (flows.md:154, accounts-switch-reading.test.ts). Neither covers the balance reading across a wallet switch. No backlog line, Not fixed list or Declined item names it. The backlog's ❓ 'public balances across a lock' is a different question (keeping balances at rest).

checked_ok: vault.ts:33-59 with secret-box/: the vault is SBV1. Argon2id (m=19456, t=2, p=1) derives a 32-byte key under a fresh 32-byte salt, and ChaCha20-Poly1305 seals under a fresh 12-byte nonce on every seal. The 48-byte header is the AAD (format.ts:68-80, open.ts:21). The derived key and the password bytes are zeroed. The AEAD tag is the password check. Plaintext is the entropy alone; no derived key is stored.

wallet.ts:277-306 and :736-763: the unlock back-off is enforced in the worker, inside the serial queue so concurrent tries can't race it, and kept in local storage across restarts. Reveal phrase, the dApp password check and change password count toward it too. A clock moved back never shortens it (:762).

wallet.ts:449-461: a password change reseals the same entropy under a fresh salt in one chrome.storage.local key write. A crash before the write leaves the old password working. The store key comes from the entropy, so every sealed record stays readable either way, and the old vault's createdAt goes.

wallet.ts:551-563 and private-store.ts:90-158: the record key is HKDF-SHA-256 of the entropy with its own salt and info, zeroed after each use. Each write takes a fresh 24-byte XChaCha nonce, the AAD binds the record name (network included), and records are padded to 1 KiB or the next power of two.

wallet.ts:615-655: auto-lock locks past the idle window, with a 30 s clock-step tolerance. Activity comes only from the wallet's own pages (App.tsx:92-100, ui/background.ts:114-125); handlers.ts:184-185 is the only touch(), so a site's CIP-30 calls never keep the wallet unlocked. A browser restart (no session entropy) frees the keys and stops the alarm.

wallet.ts:698-730: lock clears session storage before freeing, keeping only the two send times and the declined sites. The keys are dropped before their free(), and each free is in its own try. Lock frees all three key objects and every other account's.

wallet.ts:598-609 with wasm.ts:71-83 and the generated glue (wasm/pkg/seedelf_wasm.js): after a trap the wallet wipes and frees its keys before __wbg_reset_state. The finalizers compare the instance id, and every other wasm object (tx-view.ts:234-242, balances.ts:493-504, contract-scan.ts:207-212, wallet.ts:486-496) is made and freed in one synchronous scope. So no stale pointer is freed into the new instance.

wasm crate lib.rs:5730-5815, 5856-5862, 5995-6001, 6513-6548: SeedelfKey wipes its scalar on drop (volatile write). The entropy and phrase arguments are taken by value into Zeroizing, and derivation.rs returns Zeroizing values. This matches the crypto review #12 and the launch review #32.

accounts.ts:123-126 and shared/preferences.ts:68-73: an unsealed LOCAL_ACCOUNT, or a dappAccount that is 24301' or past 2^31-1, reads as account 0 or is ignored. The one-time accounts never become the public account.

handlers.ts:122-171: create and restore put the wallet on account 0 before deriving. pending and lovejoin adoptKept run before anything else reads the records. Restore marks every network unscanned before its scan starts.

Remove wallet (wallet.ts:473-480, handlers.ts:254-282) deletes the vault, the failure count, the settings, every private record but the two kept ones, and every local cache. Every local key the code writes is accounted for: network, account, language and openIn are kept on purpose, and koiosOnly is put back. git log -p of private-store.ts shows no record name was ever dropped from PRIVATE_RECORDS.
storage-access.ts:225-245 and sw.ts:59-60: local and session storage are set to TRUSTED_CONTEXTS at every start, and the connector stays off unless local storage took it.
ui-port.ts: replies, including the phrase and password requests, go only on the asking page's own port, and only to this extension's pages. Broadcasts carry nothing.

App.tsx:146-170: a lock, whatever its cause, shows Unlock and unmounts Settings, so a shown phrase (Settings.tsx:1313-1372) or a typed one (CheckPhrase) is dropped. PhraseGrid.tsx:10 renders dots, not words, while hidden. The phrase inputs have spellcheck and autocomplete off, and a pasted phrase clears the clipboard (PhraseInput.tsx:91). history.ts keeps only a marker, never form contents.
wallet.ts:415-429: the phrase check is constant-time, needs the wallet unlocked, and says only yes or no.

Heuristic scans (scratch scripts e4a_nested_scan2.py, e4a_network_in_queue.py; comments and strings stripped) found no wallet-queue call nested inside a withKeys, withAccount or withStoreKey task, and no Koios or fetch call awaited inside one. A nested call would deadlock the queue, and with it auto-lock.
delete-phrase.ts: Remove wallet and Forgot password use one NFKC-folded check of the typed words (the language's own or English), so neither accepts what the other refuses.
Create.tsx and Restore.tsx: nothing is written until the password step, and the phrase is cleared from state on success. The worker enforces the 12-character rule the UI shows (wallet.ts:259, 451).
notes: The generated glue's explicit free() (wasm/pkg/seedelf_wasm.js, e.g. CardanoAccount.free: __destroy_into_raw() then wasm.__wbg_cardanoaccount_free(ptr, 0)) has no stale-instance check. Every method has one ('Invalid stale object from previous Wasm instance'), and the finalizers compare the instance id. No harm today: the wallet frees its keys before freshWasm, and every other wasm object is freed in the same synchronous scope. A future change that holds a Register, Proof or key across an await and frees it after a reset would free an old-instance pointer into the new instance's heap. Worth a line in wasm.ts or a guarded free wrapper.

handlers.ts:126-130 calls networkChoice.keep and accounts.useFirst() before wallet.create() checks for an existing vault. A stray create-wallet or restore-wallet while a wallet exists would put that wallet on account 0 without the switch's wipe (accounts.ts WIPED_ON_SWITCH), so account N's kept reading would show as Account 1's until a Refresh. It can't fire on its own: only a page still on onboarding after the state broadcast could send it, and pages leave onboarding at the broadcast. Moving both calls after the vault check (or into Wallet.create) closes it.

vault.ts:52-58: every failure inside SecretBox.open becomes WrongPasswordError and counts toward the back-off. That includes one that isn't the tag, such as Argon2id's 19 MiB allocation failing under memory pressure, or a damaged body. A damaged vault reads as a forgotten password. Forgot password is still the way out, so this is wording only.

e4a#1 overlaps E6 (balances.ts, activity.ts) and E3 (dapp.ts view()'s shared reading map). I reported it from the Remove wallet → restore side, which is this lane's. privacy.md:269 says Remove wallet deletes every sealed record but two. That stays true of the deletion, but e4a#1 can re-create the old wallet's private arrivals inside the new wallet's sealed history, which D1 may want to know if no fix lands.

sw.ts:443-458: the auto-lock alarm can lock only after getContext() loads WebAssembly. A worker whose WebAssembly won't load leaves the session entropy in place until a later request succeeds. That needs a load failure, such as memory pressure, after an unlock; updates and browser restarts clear session storage anyway. No finding.

Not checked here and out of scope: whether Chrome keeps the TRUSTED_CONTEXTS level across a browser restart before the worker sets it again. A content script that read local storage in that window would need a compromised renderer.
